scope: Shared native Pull/Fetch editable URL and branch histories, source insertion/load/save rules, failure persistence and URL-mode Rebase gate. Partial parity; full application port remains incomplete.

verification.core: All 11 selected Fetch/Pull tests passed (6 Fetch, 5 Pull), including tracking/refspec/tag/prune/depth/all-remotes defaults, fetched Rebase snapshots and dirty-state preservation, replay ancestry, active-session rejection, merge/no-commit/squash/conflict/ff-only and URL/configuration behavior. Core implementation unchanged in this checkpoint.
verification.native: Final headless receiver passed system Git and Git 2.37.1, 2.39.5 and bundled 2.55.0. Failed URL Fetch saves trimmed shared URL/branch history before transport while HEAD/index stay byte-identical. A reopened native Pull restores that URL, then actually pulls a newly pushed commit from another literal URL with ff-only; forced programmatic launchRebase=true still cannot launch Rebase in URL mode. New Fetch in a different repository restores both histories. Branch browse selection updates in-memory history without saving; named Fetch does not persist unused URL text. Direct source-rule assertions cover ordering/case-sensitive URL and case-insensitive branch deduplication, first-entry spelling, exact UTF-16 URL identity, CR/LF folding, and 26-save/25-load. A real hidden NSComboBox has ordered items, retained typed text and working native selection callback; owned window closed. These are model/Git/hidden-control checks, not physical popup/text-input/completion or screenshots.
